rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's eighteen builder trees go (magnolias, ficus, eucalyptus and jacarandas along the back fences, queen palms and a norfolk pine 2.7-3.1 m from the houses, corals and jacarandas by the seating); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the swing set, two sets of adirondack chairs, on the open lot corner, and one back yard.

trees.why: the south back yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): a young eucalyptus over the swings
the yard with the adirondack chair (1.9 m off): a jacaranda to sit under
the west yard with the two adirondack chairs: shade for them
the open lot corner at the north-east, 24 m from the walls: a eucalyptus with room to grow
the south-west back yard, 7 m from the house: the yard's tree
